title: Verify the write
lesson: A stale verification read is not proof that a write failed: check the committed revision through a fresh authoritative read before taking another action.
limitations: Illustrative single-writer sequence; timings are not measured replica lag.
Primary verification assumes a fresh post-commit query, no intervening cache, and an available primary.
Application revisions and HOLD policy are proposed tool design, not automatic model or database guarantees.
Does not demonstrate failover, concurrent writers, synchronous replication modes, external deployment completion, or permission enforcement.
Audio was analyzed numerically and visually, not physically listened to.
Self-reviewed; independent comparative ranking and editorial promotion remain separate.

transcript.text: An agent tool reads a caught-up replica. Version 7 returns and matches the current state; no write has been made.
One write commits version 8 on the primary. The acknowledgement makes the agent expect version 8, while the replica still holds version 7.
Verification reads the replica and receives version 7. The tool shows the mismatch and holds further action; it does not repeat the write. Attention shifts to the primary.
A fresh primary read returns version 8, matching the acknowledged revision. Verification succeeds even though the replica is still behind. This example assumes one writer and no intervening cache.
Replication later applies version 8 on the replica. The write count remains one. The scene fades to its matching dark endpoint; the illustrated delay is not a latency guarantee.
